questions.q: In "Who needs this, and who is your first user Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: The mentor agrees the evidence you will produce in this course (listed at the end of each lesson).
Talk to 3 to 5 possible users or experts. Ask: what do you do now, what is hard, what would make you trust a new service?
Write a 90-day next-step plan: what to do, where, how much, what to learn next. Pick a follow-on course from the catalogue.
Churn: 50 start, 10 stop in month 1 = 20%. Average stay about 5 months. Lifetime income per buyer about 5 x 7.7 = 38.5 margin (same currency).

questions.q: In "Kick-off circle Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Pick one theme and one buyer. Write the promise in one sentence: what arrives, how often, why it is worth the price.
Peers play an unhappy buyer and ask why they should not cancel.
Peers ask three questions: who is it for, why you, what could go wrong.
Make 5 sample boxes. Time the packing of each. Weigh each box and price its delivery.

questions.q: In "Start the practice task Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: After 2 weeks, ask each buyer 3 questions: what did you like, what would make you cancel, what would you add.
Write a half-page idea: who, what you will do, what success looks like in numbers.
Offer the box to 10 people for a one-month paid test on our own pay page (test mode).
Take the 10-question check. Pass mark is 70% (draft).

questions.q: In "Short modules Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Present to a review room: idea, task record, numbers, risks, decision.
Idea: a monthly tea-and-snack box for office workers. Promise: 4 small items, delivered on the first Monday, price 30.
Give two peers written feedback: one thing that is strong, one thing to fix.
Logistics: weight bands change delivery price. Pick the box size just under a price band. Plan for what happens when an address is wrong or a box is lost.
